articles.title: NDRRMC: 8.4 million people affected by monsoon, cyclones
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Around 8.4 million individuals have been affected by the southwest monsoon and recent cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Around 8.4 million individuals have been affected by the southwest monsoon and recent cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) said on Sunday.

In its latest update as of 6 p.m., the NDRRMC said the weather systems affected 8.4 million individuals, or 2.4 million families, in the National Capital Region, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, Cordillera Administrative Region, Bicol Region, and Zamboanga Peninsula.
Approximately 122,500 individuals, or 35,500 families, are seeking temporary shelter in 1,115 evacuation centers.
The NDRRMC also reported 32 deaths linked to the weather disturbances, most of them in Benguet due to landslides. Nineteen individuals were injured, while three remained missing.

The agency estimated the total cost of damage to infrastructure and agriculture at P6.16 billion and P2.32 billion, respectively. It also said P1.7 billion worth of assistance had been provided to affected families.
A state of calamity has been declared in 117 areas in Pangasinan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.

Meanwhile, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Tropical Depression Pilandok is not forecast to make landfall over the country but will enhance the southwest monsoon, bringing more rain.

Pagasa said monsoon rains are forecast over Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, some parts of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon), and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan). /mcm

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — The Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando in Pampanga’s capital city suspended all Masses on Sunday, Aug. 30, due to flooding.
In a Facebook post late Saturday, the cathedral said floodwaters and silt had seeped into the church, while its patio and surrounding streets remained submerged.
“For the safety of all, we regret to announce that all Sunday morning and afternoon Masses tomorrow (August 30) are cancelled,” it said.
Four Masses were scheduled from 5 a.m. to 10:30 a.m., while three others were set between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.
Masses on Friday and Saturday had also been canceled due to flooding in downtown San Fernando.
Meanwhile, SM City Pampanga, which straddles San Fernando and Mexico, and SM City San Fernando Downtown also remained closed on Sunday due to flooding.
“For the safety of our customers and employees, SM City San Fernando Downtown and SM City Pampanga will be closed today, August 30, 2026,” the malls said in separate Facebook posts. /mcm

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet death toll rises amid new flood fears and race to free group trapped in tunnel
articles.summary: Combined toll of more than 750 dead and 3,000 people missing in Nepal and Tibet after devastating flood

blocks.text: Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet have battled through leg-sucking mud amid the threat of fresh flooding to search for thousands of people still missing after a deadly wall of water swept through the Himalayan border zone, engulfing entire villages.

The latest updates on Sunday put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There were 768 confirmed deaths, and reports of some bodies swept downstream possibly as far as India.

Nepal said it had begun the grim task of burying some of the hundreds of bodies after first taking DNA samples so that families could later reclaim them and perform traditional funeral rites after identification.
The disaster, which struck the border on Wednesday morning, was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
Nepal’s foreign minister called for a global response to the climate crisis, saying the small, poor Himalayan nation was bearing a disproportionate share of its impact.
“Despite having only 0.1% contribution to the global emissions, people of Nepal have become major victims of climate change,” Shisir Khanal said on Saturday.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far. Chinese authorities on Sunday reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, of whom 261 were foreign nationals, including 104 from Nepal, 49 from India, 33 from Latvia, 18 from the US and 15 British citizens.
In a breakthrough at the weekend, Nepal’s army was able to insert a pipe into a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site where more than 100 workers are believed to be trapped.
The home minister, Sudan Gurung, said: “We have already started sending air through the small opening, and we will now begin excavation work and send the rescue team inside.”

It is a race against time to reach the workers, who may still be alive inside the tunnels, with rescue efforts focused on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites. They are among 933 hydropower workers who are among the missing, according to Nepal’s disaster authority.

blocks.caption: Soldiers search for bodies as rescue operations shift into search and retrieval in Nepal.  Photograph: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images

blocks.text: Nepal warned on Sunday of rising flood waters and urged rescue teams to exercise caution. “We have received information that the flood flow in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa has increased further,” the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
Flood warnings were sent to people’s phones early on Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas hit by the devastating floods.

In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some people began returning to ruined homes to see what could be salvaged. Residents of the flood-hit villages said they were struggling to make sense of near-constant alarms they had received since the initial floods.

One resident, Govind Shreshta, told the Associated Press: “Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain. It’s really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mum. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It’s going on like this for those who are still alive.”
The government estimated Nepal’s reconstruction bill could run into the billions of dollars.
Officials in Nepal called for forensic testing kits to identify bodies and freezer units to store them in, saying bodies that had been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
Survivors face an agonising wait to learn the fate of missing relatives and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” Buddhi Ram Dangol told Agence France-Presse in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. “There is nothing left.”

blocks.caption: Firefighters conduct search and rescue operations along a river in Gyirong county in Tibet. Photograph: cnsphoto/Reuters

blocks.text: In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, rescue operations were temporarily paused at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of more flooding from a newly formed lake.
A total of 2,141 rescuers were near the Gyirong site, the Xinhua state news agency reported, including more than 500 in the worst-hit area.
In Kathmandu, Nepal’s capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning desperately searching for news of missing loved ones.
Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital noticeboard, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients’ lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had travelled from Ramechhap, about 80 miles (130km) away.
“I came here with the hope that I might find him,” she told the Associated Press. “There is no information about him.”
Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa. “I feel hopeless. It has already been four days,” she said.
With Associated Press, Agence France-Presse and Reuters

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City has fallen below its overflow level but remains above the critical level, according to the state weather bureau on Sunday evening.

In its latest update issued at 6 p.m., the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the dam’s water level stood at 80.11 meters as of 5 p.m., below the overflow elevation of 80.15 m but still above the critical level of 79.50 m.
The water level had slightly eased from 80.30 m recorded at 5 a.m. on Sunday.

Pagasa warned that excess floodwaters from the dam would flow directly into the Tullahan River, affecting low-lying areas in Quezon City (Fairview, Forest Hills Subdivision, Quirino Highway, Sta. Quiteria, and San Bartolome), Caloocan City, Valenzuela City (North Expressway and La Huerta Subdivision), Malabon City, and Navotas City.
It added that light to moderate rains were still expected over the watershed area for the next 12 hours.
“All residents living in the aforementioned areas, especially those residing near the riverbanks, are still advised to take appropriate actions,” the weather bureau noted.
In its separate 5 p.m. weather forecast, Pagasa said Tropical Depression Pilandok was not forecast to make landfall in the country but would enhance the southwest monsoon, or habagat.

It added that monsoon rains were forecast over Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, some parts of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon), and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan). /mcm

articles.title: Jorge Araneta honored for a lifetime of shaping cities
articles.summary: A meaningful career in shaping cities is reflected in the places that stand the test of time and the communities that grow around them. Jorge L. Araneta’s career reflects both, while introducing new…

blocks.text: Property and Living
Araneta Group chairman receives the Life Achievement Award at the 14th PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards for his contributions to the country's evolving urban landscape

A meaningful career in shaping cities is reflected in the places that stand the test of time and the communities that grow around them. Jorge L. Araneta’s career reflects both, while introducing new approaches to how urban spaces are planned and experienced. His long-standing contribution was recognized with the Life Achievement Award at the 14th PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards.

As chairman and CEO of the Araneta Group, Araneta has led the company through decades of growth across urban development, entertainment, sustainability, and community initiatives. Under his leadership, Araneta City expanded into a destination for commerce, culture, and entertainment, with projects such as Cyberpark Towers adding to the district. His work also includes the shift toward renewable energy and community programs through the J. Amado Araneta Foundation.

Accepting the award on his behalf was Rowell Recinto, senior management consultant of Araneta City, who highlighted several concepts that were ahead of their time. These included bringing entertainment and retail together, incorporating public transportation into development planning even before the MRT and LRT, and introducing new types of land use in Cubao.

Recinto also shared that Araneta wanted to share the recognition with the men and women of the Araneta Group, acknowledging their role in the company’s achievements. He then highlighted several ideas that have since become part of modern estate development.

“He has done this very quietly. Araneta is not the type who will go out and seek publicity, but I thought it was just fair that I mentioned a few of those pioneering planning concepts that seem to be part of everybody’s checklist in developing estates today,” Recinto said.

The Life Achievement Award adds another milestone to Araneta’s long career, recognizing contributions that have remained relevant as the industry continues to change. His work offers a lasting example of how new ideas can shape the future of urban development.

blocks.text: World·New
Rescue crews are on scene after a ferry carrying more than 260 passengers capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday.
Rescue crews are on scene
A ferry carrying more than 260 passengers capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, Turkish media reported.
The catamaran-style ferry was travelling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, in the breakaway north of ethnically divided Cyprus, to the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province.
There are no reports of casualties so far.
The ferry started taking in water a few kilometres off the coast, the Turkish state-run TRT news channel reported.
Northern Cyprus Transportation Minister Erhan Arikli told TRT that the ship had overturned and that rescue crews were already on the scene.
Several companies run ferries on the busy route between Kyrenia and Tasucu. It is not yet known which company was operating the ferry that capsized.
Video footage from the scene shows people with life-vests floating in the waters around the capsized vessel.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau votes to reshape presidency
articles.summary: The West African nation's military government wants to amend the constitution to give more powers to the president. The junta, which seized power last year, says it will hold elections in December.

image.caption: More than 900,000 people are eligible to take part in the referendumImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: Guinea-Bissau voted on Sunday in a referendum on whether to give the president new powers as the country prepares to transition from military to democratic rule.
The tiny West African nation of around 2.2 million people has been under army rule since last November following a disputed election.
What will the referendum decide?
Guinea-Bissau's junta has unanimously approved a constitutional amendment to switch the country from what it frames as a parliamentary to a presidential system.
This means abandoning the old system where the prime minister came from the parliamentary majority.
The amendment would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and dissolve parliament.
If passed, the new constitution will cut the number of seats in parliament from 102 to 65.
The junta says the change seeks to stabilize institutions before new presidential and parliamentary elections, scheduled for December 6, which are meant to hand power back to civilians.
Opposition groups, however, have urged the public to boycott the vote, saying it will allow the junta leader to cement power and calling it a "source of political instability at all levels."

blocks.caption: Guinea-Bissau is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections in DecemberImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: When are the results due?
Polls close at 1700 GMT on Sunday, with the first provisional results due from Tuesday.
One of the world's poorest countries, Guinea-Bissau has experienced five coups and a series of attempted coups since 1974.
A military government seized power in November following a disputed election in which former President Umaro Sissoco Embalo and opposition candidate Fernando Dias both claimed victory.
After legislative elections in 2023, Embalo himself dissolved the opposition-dominated parliament in response to what he described as an attempted coup.

articles.title: Pilandok to bring more rain as it enhances southwest monsoon
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok is expected to strengthen the southwest monsoon, although it is not forecast to make landfall, the state weather bureau said Sunday. In its 5 p.m.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok is expected to strengthen the southwest monsoon, although it is not forecast to make landfall, the state weather bureau said Sunday.

In its 5 p.m. weather forecast, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Luzon and western portions of Visayas would continue to experience rains due to the monsoon.

“While this will be far [from the landmass], I repeat that this will enhance the southwest monsoon, which is why we will still experience heavy rains and gusts of wind in a large portion of the country. Heavy rains are forecast over Luzon and some portions, particularly western portions of Visayas,” Pagasa weather specialist Daniel Villamil said.

Villamil added that monsoon rains were forecast over Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, some parts of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon), and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan).
Pilandok was 1,180 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon as of 4 p.m. It was carrying maximum winds of 45 kilometers per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 55 kph.
Villamil said Pilandok would generally move northwestward from Sunday until Tuesday. Its track is far from the Philippine landmass, and it is expected to weaken into a low-pressure area by Tuesday.
Aug. 31 weather forecast
Villamil said monsoon rains would still prevail over the western sections of Northern and Central Luzon on Monday, particularly in Ilocos Region, Zambales, Bataan, Abra, and Benguet.
Occasional rains would also continue over the western sections of Southern Luzon, Metro Manila, and Occidental Mindoro.

Meanwhile, weather conditions were expected to generally improve over Western Visayas, while the rest of Visayas and Mindanao would see partly cloudy to cloudy skies with chances of isolated rain showers.

articles.title: DOT eyes bringing Mindanao into PH tourism circuit
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY — The Department of Tourism (DoT) is keen on bringing Mindanao into the country’s tourism circuit, citing the island’s stable security conditions, rich cultural heritage, unique…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY — The Department of Tourism (DoT) is keen on bringing Mindanao into the country’s tourism circuit, citing the island’s stable security conditions, rich cultural heritage, unique culinary offerings, and ecotourism destinations and adventures.

Tourism Assistant Secretary Ferdinand Jose Bagcal recently led a DoT team in conducting a comprehensive validation of tourism attractions in the Zamboanga Peninsula, the results of which will be included in the national travel and tourism circuit.
He noted that the initiative, which included site validations in Zamboanga del Sur, aims to uncover new destinations beyond the country’s famed beaches.

“We want to focus on Mindanao this time because it is rich in exceptional tourist assets. Our goal is to link these destinations into cohesive circuits (in the Philippines) that travelers can easily navigate,” Bagcal explained.
Bagcal expressed optimism about this city’s tourism potential, citing the newly opened Pagadian City Water Park along the boulevard as a promising development.
“Pagadian is something waiting to be discovered. It has immense potential to emerge as a major destination,” he said.

The team’s itinerary included visits to the Sto. Niño Cathedral, the Tourism Boat, the Regional Government Center, the Provincial Government Center, the sandbar called Puting Balas, and Bakilid Resort.
Bagcal stressed that culture and heritage form a core part of the validation, with the delegation engaging the Subanen indigenous community in the towns of Kumalarang and Lakewood.
In Kumalarang, the team observed traditional weaving and handicraft-making and met with local officials led by Mayor Ruel Molina.

The delegation also visited Lakewood, home to the province’s largest freshwater lake, spanning 800 hectares at the foot of Mt. Serongan and Mt. Imbing. The site is being positioned as a scenic ecotourism destination.
Sara Mae Lee Monroy, DoT’s lead project officer for cultural tourism, emphasized the richness of Zamboanga del Sur’s tourism assets.
“We saw traditions, performances, and crafts that offer immersive experiences. Even simple mat weaving is something travelers should witness firsthand,” she said.
Monroy stressed that showcasing Mindanao’s warmth and diversity is vital to counter negative perceptions.
“Mindanao is safe, relaxing, and full of unique food and adventure. There is more to the Philippines than Boracay, Davao, or Bohol—Zamboanga Peninsula deserves a place on the tourism map,” she said.
Bagcal commended the local government units for investing in tourism infrastructure and product development, also citing the willingness of the tri-people to develop tourism in the area. /mcm

articles.title: DPWH stops projects tied to alleged illegal reclamation in Taguig City
articles.summary: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders (CDOs) covering projects linked to the alleged illegal reclamation of portions of Laguna de Bay in Taguig City,…

blocks.text: (MB FILE PHOTO)

The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders (CDOs) covering projects linked to the alleged illegal reclamation of portions of Laguna de Bay in Taguig City, DPWH Secretary Vivencio “Vince” Dizon confirmed on Sunday, Aug. 30.
Dizon said the orders were issued on Aug. 20 upon the directive of the Office of the President through the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA).

“We already issued the CDOs, as ordered by the Office of the President through the Philippine Reclamation Authority. Kasi ang PRA, under the Office of the President ‘yan (This is because the PRA is under the Office of the President),” Dizon told reporters during his visit to Marikina City.
“So, nag-issue na kami [ng CDOs] noong August 20 (So, we already issued the CDOs on Aug. 20),” he added.
The DPWH chief said the stakeholders, including the Taguig City government, Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA), and PRA, would hold a meeting to discuss the issues surrounding the projects.

“Nagpatawag na ng meeting ang iba’t ibang stakeholders kasama na ang City of Taguig plus LLDA and PRA (The various stakeholders, including the City of Taguig, the LLDA, and the PRA, have already called a meeting),” he said.

“Let’s just discuss it kung ano ba talaga, kung mayroong mga problema dyan (Let’s just discuss what the situation really is and whether there are problems there). Aalamin natin kung ano ‘yung way forward (We will determine the way forward). But lahat ‘yan, effective immediately (But all of those are effective immediately),” Dizon added.

On Aug. 10, Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said the PRA had informed him, his staff, and DPWH officials that all reclaimed areas in Taguig City without PRA permits, whether held by the local government or private individuals or corporate entities, were subject to forfeiture in favor of the national government.

He said the PRA and DPWH had also agreed that the DPWH would begin issuing cease-and-desist orders covering ongoing slope protection and mitigation projects in the area following the discovery of 32 anomalous and suspected ghost projects.
As such, Lacson said the facts established by his team and validated by the concerned agencies contradicted Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano’s denials during his Facebook Live broadcasts.

articles.summary: Several people have died after a passenger ⁠boat carrying more than 260 people capsized off ‌northern Cyprus, Turkish media reported. ‌

image.caption: The ferry capsized shortly after departing from the Northern Cyprus port of KyreniaImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: A passenger ferry capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, shortly after leaving port, the local government said.
At least seven people have died, Turkish state media reported, citing Unal Ustel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC).
Ustel said that some 237 people had been rescued.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974, with the northern part under the administration of the TRNC, which is recognized internationally only by Turkey.

blocks.caption: Authorities said many of the passengers and crew members were rescuedImage: Reuters TV/REUTERS

blocks.text: Passenger boat heading from northern Cyprus to Turkey

Turkish media reported that a ferry carrying more than 260 passengers was traveling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, to the Turkish port of Tasucu in southern Mersin province, when it sank.
Erhan Arikli, the TRNC's Transport Minister, told Turkish and Cypriot media that there were 267 people on board — 259 passengers and 8 crew members.
"All necessary preparations are being made for a swift response from rescue and health services," the TRNC's Health Ministry said in a statement.
Search and rescue operations ongoing

articles.title: NCDA calls for due process in incident involving PWD, security guard
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) called for due process after a person with disability (PWD) was involved in an incident with a security guard at a bookstore in…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) called for due process after a person with disability (PWD) was involved in an incident with a security guard at a bookstore in a mall in Quezon City.
In a statement on Sunday, the NCDA “recommended that establishments ensure due process, fair treatment, and coordination with law enforcement in handling cases.”
The NCDA sent a staff member to speak with store management, which confirmed that the PWD had allegedly attempted to take items and place them in a bag on several occasions.
According to the NCDA, store management said the person had not been discriminated against or banned from the store.
Bookstore personnel also reported previous incidents in which the individual allegedly harmed security guards and employees.
“Illegal acts like theft must go through legal channels with due process,” the NCDA said.

According to the SM North Edsa Customer Relations Services (CRS) office, the security guard seen in the viral video has been placed under preventive suspension while the incident is under investigation.
The NCDA recommended verifying the individual’s identity in coordination with the local Persons with Disability Affairs Office for possible intervention.
SM CRS will provide the NCDA with the agency’s full incident report once completed.
“Security measures must be reasonable, non-discriminatory, and respectful of dignity at all times,” the NCDA said.
The government organization stressed that persons with disabilities, like everyone else, are equal before the law and accountable for their actions.
At the same time, the NCDA warned against stereotyping or profiling persons with disabilities based on a single incident.
“Most persons with disabilities are law-abiding and contribute positively to society,” the NCDA said.
“The public is urged to avoid discrimination and profiling,” it added.
The NCDA said it will continue monitoring the case to ensure that neither discrimination nor impunity prevails.
“Justice and inclusion are not opposing values; they go hand in hand,” the NCDA said. /mcm

articles.title: Protect journalists, Filipinos’ right to the truth – Legarda
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda called for stronger protection for journalists and other media workers on Thursday, National Press Freedom Day, stressing that a free and secure press is…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda called for stronger protection for journalists and other media workers on Thursday, National Press Freedom Day, stressing that a free and secure press is essential to the public’s right to truthful, timely, and reliable information.

In a statement, Legarda pointed out that the Philippines ranked 114th out of 180 countries in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index of Reporters Without Borders (RSF). While an improvement on its116th ranking in 2025, she noted that the RSF continued to describe the Philippines as one of the most dangerous countries in the world for journalists.

Unesco, she added, has also recorded cases of journalists killed in the Philippines this year.⠀Aug. 30 is observed annually as National Press Freedom Day under Republic Act No. 11699, in honor of Marcelo H. Del Pilar, the father of Philippine journalism.

The law also calls for greater awareness of the importance of the press, its rights and responsibilities, and the need to eliminate violence against journalists.⠀“When the press can investigate freely and ask difficult questions without fear, Filipinos are better able to know where public funds go, whether laws are being followed, and whether government programs are working. A free press gives citizens the verified information they need to hold institutions and public officials accountable,” Legarda, an award-winning broadcast journalist before entering public service, stressed.⠀Journalism now, she said, faces a more serious challenge as it deals with online misinformation, disinformation, fabricated content, misleading headlines, and unverified claims.

“With the reach and speed of social media, a false statement can spread farther and faster than the truth. That makes credible journalism even more important. Speed does not replace verification, virality does not replace evidence, and repetition does not turn an allegation into a fact,” she said.
Same discipline for public officials
The same discipline should guide public officials and government institutions, she added.

“When a government institution speaks, people expect its statements to be based on verified information. Public institutions, therefore, have a responsibility to distinguish an allegation from an established finding and to avoid language that creates a presumption of guilt before the evidence has been properly examined,” Legarda said.
She warned that trial by publicity can damage public trust in institutions and in the media.

“The public deserves to know what has been verified, what remains an allegation, and what evidence actually exists. Journalism serves the people when those distinctions are maintained. Government institutions should exercise the same care in the information they release,” she said.
Stronger labor protection

Legarda also renewed her push for stronger labor protection for media workers through Senate Bill No. 807, or the proposed Media Workers Welfare Act, which seeks to improve the working conditions, security, and benefits of media workers.

“A reporter covering a typhoon, an armed conflict, a fire, or a disaster performs work that directly serves the public. That reporter is also a worker with a family to support and a life that deserves protection. We cannot expect journalists to remain on the frontlines while ignoring the risks they face in doing their jobs,” Legarda said.

“The provincial reporter investigating a local anomaly, the radio journalist reporting from a remote municipality, the photographer documenting a disaster, and the community journalist giving voice to people who are rarely heard should be able to work safely and with dignity,” she added.
Journalists must remain free to investigate those in power, she stressed, while public officials and institutions must ensure that the information they release is supported by facts and evidence.

“Protecting press freedom means protecting journalists who pursue the truth even when it is difficult or inconvenient. Let us protect the journalist who seeks the truth, protect the citizen who deserves the truth, and protect our institutions from being used to distort the truth,” Legarda said. /atm

articles.title: 2 suspects killed in Lanao police op; infant dies in grenade blast
articles.summary: MARAWI CITY, Lanao del Sur — Two men were killed in a firefight between police and armed suspects during a warrant implementation here late Saturday, while a six-month-old infant later died after a…

blocks.text: MARAWI CITY, Lanao del Sur — Two men were killed in a firefight between police and armed suspects during a warrant implementation here late Saturday, while a six-month-old infant later died after a grenade allegedly left by the fleeing target exploded.

Capt. Steffi Salanguit, spokesperson for the Police Regional Office Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (PROBAR), said the operation was launched around 11 p.m. in Barangay Tampilong to serve an arrest warrant against Kadapi Mimbesa Mortiaba, who is facing a case for alleged violation of the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020.
The warrant was issued by a court in Iligan City, Lanao del Norte, and dated Oct. 11, 2024. It carried no recommended bail, the police reported.
Police said the operating team was approaching the target’s location when an armed individual spotted them and suddenly opened fire.
The suspects allegedly continued firing at the law enforcers, triggering an exchange of gunfire.
Mortiaba managed to escape during the encounter, while two of his alleged companions were killed.
Police identified the fatalities as Saidamen Darimbang Ali, alias “Mohaimen Hadji Ali Darimbang,” and Nesren Camar Solaiman. Both were adults, married and residents of Barangay Bangon in Marawi City.
Police said a suspected grenade allegedly left behind by Mortiaba subsequently exploded, injuring a six-month-old infant.
The baby was rushed to a hospital for medical treatment but was later declared dead, according to the police report.

The operation was led by the Lanao del Sur Police Provincial Office, with support from the 1403rd Regional Mobile Force Battalion, 1st Provincial Mobile Force Company, Provincial Intelligence Unit, Provincial Explosive Ordnance and Canine Unit, Task Force Marawi, the Army’s 103rd Infantry Brigade, and the Marawi City Police Station.
Authorities continued to pursue Mortiaba, who remained at large after the encounter. /mcm

articles.title: For labor group, NCR wage hike order technically in effect
articles.summary: The Association of Minimum Wage Earners and Advocates (AMWEA-PTGWO) is contending that the minimum wage increase under NCR (National Capital Region) Wage Order No. 27 is already in effect. In a…

blocks.text: The Association of Minimum Wage Earners and Advocates (AMWEA-PTGWO) is contending that the minimum wage increase under NCR (National Capital Region) Wage Order No. 27 is already in effect.

In a letter dated Aug. 27, 2026 and addressed to Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) Secretary Francis Toletino, the group urged the immediate implementation of the ₱60 increase under the wage order.

“Dahil naglapse na ang TRO at hindi naging effective ang preliminary injunction, effective na ang Wage Order No. 27. Dapat ng bayaran ng mga kumpanya ang ₱60 na umento sa minimum wage,” said AMWEA-PTGWO, a duly recognized labor organization by DOLE.
(Since the TRO has lapsed and the preliminary injunction was not effective, Wage Order No. 27 is now in effect. Companies must pay the ₱60 increase in the minimum wage.)

The group is one of the intervenors in the declaratory relief case pending with the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch No. 152, as filed by petitioners Readycon Trading and Construction Corporation and RII-Builders, Inc., and with the NCR Regional Tripartite Wage and Productivity Board (Wage Board) and the National Wages and Productivity Commission (NWPC), as respondents.

Judge Marie Joyce Manongsong, in the Order dated Aug. 13, 2026, granted the writ of preliminary injunction enjoining the Wage Board and NWPC from implementing Wage Order No. 27. However, this was predicated upon the petitioners' putting up a bond of P10 billion.

Readycon and RII-Builders were not able to put up the bond as required by the court. Instead the petitioner-companies asked for a reconsideration on the injunction bond in a Manifestation and Omnibus Motion dated Aug. 16, 2026.
In the meantime, the Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) issued last Aug. 4, 2026 already lapsed.

“Ang sabi ng motion ng Readycon at RII-Builders, napakalaki daw ng bond na 10 bilyong piso. Nagtaka sila kung bakit ang halaga ng bond ay binatay sa region wide impact ng injunction. Ito ay samantalang hindi naman sila nagsampa ng class suit para sa lahat ng mga employers sa NCR," AMWEA-PTGWO said.

(The motion of Readycon and RII-Builders said that the ₱10‑billion bond was too large. They wondered why the bond amount was based on the region‑wide impact of the injunction, even though they did not file a class suit for all employers in NCR.)

From the start, AMWEA‑PTGWO said it believed that not all workers in NCR could be covered, since they are not part of the case. This is because a declaratory relief case is an action in personam (against a persom), not in rem (against a thing).

"Ngayon ay nilinaw ng Readycon at RII-Builders na ganito nga ang kanilang intensyon sa kanilang petisyon. Hindi nila intindihin ang kalahatan ng mga manggagawa sa NCR. Ang sa kanilang konsiderasyon at interes ay ang sarili lamang nilang mga kumpanya,” the group continued.

(Now Readycon and RII‑Builders have clarified that this was indeed their intention in their petition. They do not consider all workers in NCR. Their concern and interest are only for their own companies.)

The AMWEA is affiliated with the Philippine Trade and General Workers Organization (PTGWO), the country’s biggest federation of labor unions and organizations, as officially recognized by the DOLE. AMWEA-PTGWO joined several labor groups in filing for an intervention in the said case.

"Malinaw na wala ng balakid sa pagpapatupad ng first tranche na ₱60 minimum wage increase. Nawa ay kusang loob na itong ibigay ng ating mga kumpanya sa Metro Manila. Kung hindi ay baka bahain ang DOLE at mga tanggapan nito ng mga kaso upang mabayaran ng tama ang ating mga minimum wage earners at ibang pang mga manggagawa,” it concluded.

(It is clear that there are no more obstacles to implementing the first tranche ₱60 minimum wage increase. Hopefully, companies in Metro Manila will voluntarily grant this. If not, DOLE and its offices may be flooded with cases to ensure proper payment for our minimum wage earners and other workers.)

articles.title: Australia keeps Jordan winless in fourth window of the FIBA WC
articles.summary: Australia kept Jordan winless in the fourth window of 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers with a 126-93 victory at the Mall of Asia Arena on Sunday, Aug. 30. The Boomers proved to be too much for…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Australia kept Jordan winless in the fourth window of 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers with a 126-93 victory at the Mall of Asia Arena on Sunday, Aug. 30.

blocks.text: Australia kept Jordan winless in the fourth window of 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers with a 126-93 victory at the Mall of Asia Arena on Sunday, Aug. 30.
The Boomers proved to be too much for the Falcons, racing to an early 22-7 lead and never looked back since then to stay undefeated through eight games in the qualifiers.

The Jordan loss should help the cause for Gilas Pilipinas as it gave the Filipinos the opportunity to close the gap in the standings. The Falcons fell to a 5-3 record after also losing against Gilas, 82-81.
Anthony Dell’Orso led the attack for the Boomers with 19 points while Angus Glover added 16. Josh Bannan had 15 while Elijah Pepper chipped in 14.
Amin Abu Hawwas paced Jordan with 21 while Jalen Harris and Abdullah Olajuwon added 19 apiece in a losing effort.
Meanwhile in the first game, New Zealand made it six straight wins in the qualifiers after whipping Syria, 126-74.
The Tall Blacks leaned on the triple threat of Corey Webster, Flynn Cameron and Sam Mennenga to seize the second spot of the Group E standings with a 6-2 slate.
Webster led the way with 22 points while Cameron added 21. Mennenga chipped in 20.
James Justice Jr. was the lone bright spot for Syria with 22 points. His team fell to a 2-6 record at the bottom of the standings.

articles.title: 2027 budget: Tinio warns of possible DPWH budget insertions in House GAB
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Sunday warned of possible insertions in the Department of Public Works and Highways’ (DPWH) budget in the House of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Sunday warned of possible insertions in the Department of Public Works and Highways’ (DPWH) budget in the House of Representatives’ version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

According to Tinio, the DPWH plans to submit institutional amendments to the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). He said that while the agency insists that changes to its initial budget submission are “amendments,” rather than “errata,” items not included in the NEP will still be inserted and subject to “For Later Release.”
“In short, there will be congressional—well, the usual term for that is ‘insertions.’ And amendments. So expect that there would be big changes in the GAB,” Tinio said.

The House version of the GAB was filed by Nueva Ecija Rep. Mikaela Suansing, chairperson of the House committee on appropriations. The Department of Budget and Management transmitted the P7.2-trillion 2027 NEP to the lower chamber.

The House appropriations committee held a briefing on the DPWH’s proposed P643.95-billion budget, with major allocations for foreign-assisted projects (P117.74 billion), the national road system (P199.58 billion) and local flood control projects (P83.84 billion).

Tinio said the standard timeline for completing a project stretched to at least two years, noting that only 32% of the more than 17,000 projects this year had been awarded as of the third quarter of August.

During the budget briefing, DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said that of the 17,764 infrastructure projects lined up for this year, amounting to roughly P460 billion, about 76%, or 15,032 contracts worth P349.5 billion, had been advertised for procurement.
Dizon noted that the agency had awarded 7,467 projects amounting to P146.1 billion so far. He said 80% of all pending construction projects would be awarded by September this year.
“My point being, because of this system of errata, insertions, and so on, the standard timeline for construction is really at least two years, whether the project is large or small,” Tinio said.
“Meaning, the pork barrel system is the major bottleneck to economic development and the delivery of basic services—for example, classrooms,” he added.
Tinio also said he would continue to scrutinize the DPWH’s budget, emphasizing that congressional insertions and amendments are still possible despite reforms.
The INQUIRER has sought Dizon’s comment on Tinio’s remarks and has yet to receive a response. /mcm

articles.title: PLM students question Marcos’ honorary degree, cite Hilao’s legacy
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Students of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) are questioning the university administration’s decision to confer an honorary Doctor of Laws degree on President…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Students of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) are questioning the university administration’s decision to confer an honorary Doctor of Laws degree on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
They said they were not consulted and warned that the recognition could be seen as an endorsement of an administration facing issues over good governance.

They also cited PLM’s history, invoking the memory of Liliosa Hilao, a PLM student journalist who was the first reported student activist to die in detention during martial law under the Marcos Sr. dictatorship.
Marcos on Aug. 27 received a Doctor of Laws, honoris causa (Latin for “for the sake of honor”), from PLM during the graduation rites of the city government-run university.

The university cited the president’s support for PLM, particularly the construction of the PLM Allied Health Sciences Building through the conversion and retrofitting of the old Ospital ng Maynila facility. Marcos himself attended the building’s groundbreaking ceremony in February.
Higher standards

In a joint statement on Saturday evening, the PLM Supreme Student Council, along with 33 other local student councils and organizations, assailed the resolution of the board of regents (BOR), the university’s highest policymaking body, to award an honorary degree to Mr. Marcos.

“To bestow such an honor upon a sitting president whose administration remains subject to serious questions concerning transparency, accountability, human rights, and public service risks turning an academic distinction into an endorsement of a record that remains deeply contested,” they said.
“For an institution that prides itself on Karunungan, Kaunlaran, at Kadakilaan, such recognition must be held to a standard higher than political position or institutional convenience,” they added.

To grant the recognition to Marcos without the PLM administration considering the concerns raised by the university community “risks diminishing the significance of the degree itself and disrespecting those who continue to uphold the principles of truth, accountability, and service,” their statement read.
The granting of the honorary academic degree to Marcos was also an attempt to whitewash the atrocities committed by the dictatorship of his father, Ferdinand Marcos Sr., against PLM students.

They also brought up the memory of Hilao, then a graduating communication arts student at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila and an editor of the school paper Ang Hasik, who was the first student leader to die while in detention during the martial law regime of Marcos Sr.
Aged 23, Hilao was allegedly tortured after she was abducted by Philippine Constabulary troopers in 1973.

Her body, according to her sister Alice, was “butchered, the body was unevenly cut in half up to her vagina, like that of an animal carcass; the brain was taken out, placed in a pail, the intestines were also removed, placed likewise in a pail and all organs poured with muriatic acid.”

Her lips bore cigarette burns. She had 11 injection marks on her arms and deep handcuff marks on her wrists. Her torso was badly bruised with finger marks and gun-barrel marks. It was also possible she was sexually abused.
“Her story, together with the lives of countless others who suffered, were silenced, and were taken during that dark chapter of our history, must never be forgotten or erased,” the PLM students said.
“More so, we must never forget to honor our own blood—a fellow Haribon who, like many others, became a victim of the same regime,” she added.

In a separate statement on Sunday, the PLM College of Law Student Council (CLSC) called for clarification on the conferment of the honorary Doctor of Laws degree on Mr. Marcos “in the interest of preserving the trust and credibility of PLM and the distinctions it confers.”

They questioned whether the PLM board of regents, as well as the Legal Education Board (LEB), determined if President Marcos’ academic credentials satisfy the educational qualification under LEB Memorandum Order (MO) No. 033, series of 2025.
Under Section 4(d) of the LEBMO, a prospective honoree “must have have at least a baccalaureate degree or its equivalent from a reputable institution.”
“It is not necessary for the honoree to be a lawyer or a law graduate,” the section reads.
No undergraduate degree?

While Mr. Marcos maintained that he obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in Philosophy, Politics and Economics from the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, the university had already confirmed that, based on its records, he did not complete his degree but was awarded a Special Diploma in Social Studies in 1978.

He admitted that he was not able to complete his Master of Business Administration course at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania in the United States after enrolling in 1979 because he was elected Ilocos Norte vice governor in 1980.
In 2023, Marcos also revealed that he did not finish his special diploma course in economics at the University of Asia and the Pacific (UA&P) in Pasig City.
“This inquiry is not intended to diminish the significance of the honor nor to disrespect the university administration. Neither does it prejudge the validity of the conferment,” the PLM CLSC said.

“Rather, it seeks to promote transparency and provide the PLM College of Law community with a clearer understanding of the standards and institutional processes governing the conferment of honorary degrees,” it added.
In response, PLM’s BOR chair Edward Serapio acknowledged the criticisms from the community over their decision.

“I stand by the principle that the honor was conferred in grateful recognition of the President’s support for education and for the construction of the PLM Medicine and Allied Sciences Building,” Serapio said in a statement.
“The intention was to acknowledge this tangible contribution that advances learning and strengthens opportunities for our students,” he added.

Serapio was among the founding partners of the now-defunct MOST Law Office, along with First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, former Executive Secretary Paquito Ochoa Jr. and the late corporate lawyer Joseph Tan. /mcm

articles.title: Sask. woman crowned Mrs. Canada Universe after 26 years away from the stage
articles.summary: Jasmin Esquivel of Prince Albert, Sask., won the national pageant in Surrey, B.C. and will represent Canada at the Mrs. Universe 2026 competition in Sri Lanka this fall. She says her children are her…

image.caption: Jasmin Esquivel, Mrs. Canada Universe 2026, with her children, from left to right: Reign, Brianna, JM, Rendel and Jassie. (Aisha Ashraf/CBC)

blocks.text: Saskatchewan

Jasmin Esquivel of Prince Albert, Sask., won the national pageant in Surrey, B.C. and will represent Canada at the Mrs. Universe 2026 competition in Sri Lanka this fall. She says her children are her greatest support.
Jasmin Esquivel will represent Canada at Mrs. Universe 2026 pageant in Sri Lanka
Earlier this summer, Jasmin Esquivel flew from Saskatchewan to British Columbia, unaware that her life was about to change.
Just a few days later, Esquivel was crowned Mrs. Canada Universe 2026 at the Bell Performing Arts Centre in Surrey, B.C.
“I didn't expect it, after many years, after having five kids,” Esquivel told CBC Saskatchewan.
“I realize that one day your dream is going to come true.”
Esquivel was 17 when she competed in her last pageant. When the opportunity arose to be part of this contest at 43 years old, something inside her sparked, she said.
“I think it's a memory, like it's in my blood."
Esquivel lives in Prince Albert, Sask., with her children. She said they've supported her and inspired her all the way, in spite of her own doubts about entering the competition.
“We were shocked at first,” said her eldest daughter, Brianna Balajonda.
“But then looking at her through preparing and training, it really amazed us and inspired us too.”
Esquivel said her kids are the reason she wears the national crown today. Not only are they her motivation, but they have been with her behind the curtains throughout the pageant.
“They are my reason why — why am I here and why am I wearing this gown,” she said. “They are on the back of this pageant.”
A great part of the process is about the things contestants can do for their communities, and she's happy and thankful to have such a large one, she said.
Esquival and her family started volunteering in care homes and at multiple sports events, even organizing their own fun runs, in the lead-up to the pageant.
Her goal is to remind every woman and mother that there’s always space in life for your own dreams, she said.
“There's always a perfect time for you. So after having this crown and this title, I just realized that you can still continue your dreams,” she said.
“Having kids doesn't mean we will stop.”
Sask. woman crowned Mrs. Canada Universe wants other moms to dream big too
Balajonda said she’s grateful to have been right beside her mom through the process.
“She inspires me as a woman, that even though you're still a mother, you can still pursue your dreams. Even though you have five children, you can still do what you love.”
Esquivel will head to Sri Lanka in October for Mrs. Universe 2026, representing Canada and her hometown.
Her children said they can’t wait to root for her on the next stage.
“We're here for you and we're cheering for you and we love you so much.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Andrea Vera is a Regina-based journalist. You can reach her at andrea.vera@cbc.ca.
With files from Aisha Ashraf

articles.title: Why this northern B.C. community is giving out 23-year-old toilets for free
articles.summary: The District of Port Edwards is giving away free low-flush toilets that have been sitting unused in the district office basement for the past two decades.

image.caption: Port Edward District staff members Alex Sirovyak and Chelsea Franco stand with Chief Administrative Officer Tyson Schofield as they prepare to hand out free toilets to residents. The toilets were originally part of a water conservation initiative the district ran in 2003. (Sumi Ragu/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
The District of Port Edwards is giving away free low-flush toilets that have been sitting unused in the district office basement for the past two decades.
The low-flush toilets were part of Port Edward's water conservation initiative from 2003
The small community of Port Edward just south of Prince Rupert in northwest B.C. is giving out free toilets to its residents distributed on a first-come first serve basis.
The low-flush toilets have been sitting in Port Edward's district office basement for the past two decades, leftover stock from a previous water conservation initiative in 2003.
"They're taking up a lot of space down in our basement," explained Tyson Schofield, the district's chief administrative officer.
"I thought, 'This is not a good use of these toilets. Let's get them out for their intended purpose and let's get them out to the residents what they were used for.'"
Schofield started his position with Port Edward, which had 470 residents as of the 2021 census, in June after moving from the City of Delta.
When he discovered the 35 toilets collecting dust in the office basement, he decided to revive the program and give them away for free.

On Thursday Aug. 27, the district announced on social media it would be giving away free water-reduction toilets using an image of Oprah Winfrey and the words, "You get a toilet! You get a toilet! You get a toilet!"
By the next day, 18 toilets had already been claimed by residents.
Teresa Andrews is a Port Edward resident who came to the district office to pick up a free toilet for herself and her sons' houses.
"It's a great thing for them to do for us," she said. "It means that we're upgrading our toilet without having to go to the hardware store and buy one."

Schofield said he did some research into the original 2003 program, and found Port Edward had been reconstructing its water treatment plant at the time, and to get grant money for the project the community had to lower its water usage.
"From conversation with the community back then, it came up that we could install some low-flush toilets, so that's why they were purchased," he said.

items: More stories from Northern B.C.

blocks.text: Schofield emphasized that the toilets are over 20 years old, so he can't guarantee their quality.
But he said they recently installed two of them in the district office and they've been working well.
"They might not be the perfect toilet," he said. "However, it's always good to reduce the use of water. "
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Hanna Petersen is a reporter for CBC News, working out of the Prince George, B.C., bureau. You can email her at hanna.petersen@cbc.ca.
Sumi Ragu

articles.title: Winnipeg's 1st female mayor wants to see a 2nd. That's not likely in this fall's election
articles.summary: Susan Thompson is the first — and only — woman to serve as Winnipeg's mayor. Nearly three decades after she left office, she says it's taking too long for a second woman to be sworn in.

image.caption: Susan Thompson remains the only woman to serve as Winnipeg's mayor more than 30 years after she was sworn in as the first in 1992. (Kevin Nepitabo/CBC)

blocks.text: Susan Thompson is the first woman to serve as Winnipeg's mayor. Nearly three decades after she left office, she says it's taking too long for a second to be sworn in.
"Our city is over 150 years old, and I'm still the only woman to have become mayor. We have to change that," said Thompson, who was the mayor of Manitoba's capital from 1992 until 1998.
But it doesn't appear that will change soon.
As of Saturday morning, none of the 11 people who had registered to run for mayor in the city's upcoming October election are women.
Thompson wants to see women sign up before the Sept. 22 registration deadline passes.
"It's been over 30 years since there's been a woman leader, and it is time," Thompson said.
She said her gender was often an issue for other people when she ran for office and led the city in the 1990s.
Many those issues persist today, Thompson said.
Four years ago, she told CBC News there needs to be "another seismic shift" in order to achieve gender parity at city hall.
Despite making up half of Winnipeg's population, women remain underrepresented on city council. Just 37 per cent of council seats are currently held by women.
Barriers are still excluding many women from entering — or even considering entering — the Canadian political sphere, said Kelly Saunders, a political science professor at Brandon University.
On average, women hold about one-third of elected positions across all levels of government in Canada, she said.

items: A sit down with Susan Thompson
Former Winnipeg mayor Susan Thompson still hoping to see 2nd woman in the job, but prof says obstacles remain

blocks.text: "We make up half the population in this country and in this province and in the city, so I would certainly like to see more representation of women," Saunders said.
But Saunders isn't surprised women aren't running to become Winnipeg's next mayor.
They may be choosing not to run due to the harassment, threats and personal attacks that politicians can face, both online and in person.
These attacks can be more vicious and sexist when women and other gender-diverse people run for office, Saunders said.
Last year, the Winnipeg constituency offices of Manitoba Families Minister Nahanni Fontaine and Housing Minister Bernadette Smith were targeted by vandalism and fires.

items: Manitoba MLA Nahanni Fontaine calls threatening letters she received 'grotesque' after man, 72, arrested
NDP cabinet ministers won't be pushed out of politics by 'attacks' at offices, MLA Nahanni Fontaine says

blocks.text: Smith said the incidents were an "attack on democracy" and Fontaine said the acts wouldn't scare the ministers out of politics.
Despite the hazards of working in politics, Saunders sees more and more young women filling the seats in her political science classes, she said.
'Blood sport'
"It's not that women aren't interested. It's … the fact that there are larger structural systemic barriers that make it that much harder for us to run and to be successful at running," she said.
"I think until we really address the larger problems in our political system … it's going to remain a pretty exclusive place, where a lot of people just don't feel welcome."
When Thompson first ran for public office in Winnipeg, she was warned that politics is a "blood sport."
But she worked to avoid hostility in order to focus on important issues and meeting municipal goals, she said.
She "wouldn't allow bad behaviour" while leading the city, she said.
"You want to see honesty, integrity, courage, leadership — and you want to see the job done. You don't want to see bad behaviour," Thompson said.
Waverley West Coun. Janice Lukes, a longtime fixture on Winnipeg city council, agreed that "politics is not for the faint of heart," in an interview on Up to Speed.
"It can get really nasty, but if you're dedicated and committed, you will succeed and move mountains," said Lukes, who was first elected in 2014.
Lukes decided not to run for re-election this year. In June, she told reporters that she felt she had accomplished what she set out to do when she entered municipal politics.
While she doesn't want to run for mayor, Lukes believes Winnipeg will eventually see another woman at the helm.

items: Waverley West Coun. Janice Lukes won't run for re-election
Outgoing Winnipeg councillors back candidates to succeed them as election registration opens

blocks.text: In Brandon, Manitoba's second-largest city, there are no women on the mayoral ballot either.
As of Saturday morning, only incumbent Jeff Fawcett and former Progressive Conservative MLA Len Isleifson were registered to run.
Tracy Baker works to encourage more women to run for municipal office in Brandon as one of the co-founders of Her Seat at the Table.
Ward 1 Coun. Heather Karrouze is currently the only woman on the western Manitoba city's council. That means women make up less than 10 per cent of the 11-person leadership team.
Baker said council needs more gender diversity so it can better represent Brandon's residents.

"We're just trying to have literally our seat at the table, because we think it's very important that there is, first of all, gender equality, but also the different ideas and community involvement that come from both men and women are important," she said.

Baker said more women have expressed interest in getting into local politics since the group started in 2023, but there's a lot more work ahead before women are equitably represented on Brandon's council.

Kathy Valentino, president of the Association of Manitoba Municipalities, is a city councillor in Thompson in northern Manitoba, where women make up 50 per cent of the eight-person council — led by Mayor Colleen Smook.
Valentino said anyone who is interested in making a difference in their local community should step up and register to run.
"A municipality is made up of many different people with different experiences and ideas, and that's good and that's healthy," she said. "We need all people of diverse ranges to step forward."
The Association of Manitoba Municipalities has a resource hub on its website with information for people who are interested in running in the Oct. 28 general municipal election.
Thompson has long kept an eye out for local women who would make good candidates — and she wants other Winnipeggers to do the same.

items: Susan Thompson opens up about time as Winnipeg mayor in new candid autobiography

blocks.text: "If you see somebody that would make a good candidate, you have to encourage them," the former mayor said.
"Winnipeg has wonderful women, but it really does take a village to encourage candidates.… Get in there and support and encourage women to take on the challenge."

articles.title: Ivana Alawi hits back at critics of recent relief efforts
articles.summary: Vidoes and photos of actress-influencer vana Alawi distributing relief goods on a flooded road became hot topic on social media recently. Apparently, some deemed it too performative, noting there was…

blocks.text: Ivana Alawi (Facebook)
Vidoes and photos of actress-influencer vana Alawi distributing relief goods on a flooded road became hot topic on social media recently.
Apparently, some deemed it too performative, noting there was a drier part near the same road.
Some netizens said she had actually put some of the people getting relief packs in danger doing so.
Ivana finally addressed the issue recently in the comments section.

"Sa mga nagkakalat ng hate dahil bakit hindi sa tuyong area tumigil, Sana alamin niyo din kung bakit nandoon sa gitna ng baha ang truck natin, nasiraan ito at hindi na maka andar ng bandang hapon," she wrote.

Ivana continued: "Kaya habang sinusubükan naming ayusin para lumipat sa ibang area, may mga biglang pumila at nag stop din kung saan tumirik. Bumabalik lang din kami sa area kung san natigil ang truck namin para makahakot din ng relief goods para madala sa ibang area."
Ivana urged followers not to be too quick in issuing judgement.
"Sana ay maunawaan din ang buong sitwasyon bago tayo manghusga," she concluded.

MANILA, Philippines – Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength on Sunday afternoon, August 30, and is enhancing the southwest monsoon or habagat.

In its 5 pm bulletin on Sunday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Pilandok was located 1,180 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon. It is moving northwestward slowly, with maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour and gustiness of up to 55 km/h.
PAGASA said Pilandok is seen to move west northwestward on Monday, August 31, before turning generally northwestward.

It is less likely to make landfall and is expected to be a short-lived tropical cyclone, remaining a tropical depression before weakening into a remnant low over the Philippine Sea south of the southern islands of Japan on Tuesday, September 1.

articles.title: Four missing after Agana Bridge collapse; search operations continue
articles.summary: Tarlac City -— Search, rescue and retrieval operations continued Sunday for four individuals who remained missing following the collapse of Agana Bridge at around 7:40 p.m. on Aug. 29. The city…

blocks.text: Tarlac City -— Search, rescue and retrieval operations continued Sunday for four individuals who remained missing following the collapse of Agana Bridge at around 7:40 p.m. on Aug. 29.

The city government of Tarlac identified the missing individuals as Paul Harvey Collado, James Patrick Taborlupa, Shiela Mae Taborlupa, and Shonen Tuhaw, who were among the five occupants of an Asian utility vehicle (AUV) that was swept away after the incident.
Nathaniel Dizon, the fifth occupant, was rescued by response teams following the incident. Authorities are continuing efforts to locate the four missing individuals.
Personnel from the CDRRMO, PDRRMO, FIL-CHI, 3rd Mechanized Infantry Battalion, TOG 3, 522nd, 7CMOBN, PNP, VAT, SCAN, and DELTA COMM are participating in the ongoing search operation.
The deployment of boats and floating devices, however, remains difficult because of heavy rains and strong, fast-moving currents, which pose risks to the rescuers.
It has also limited the use of available drones, further challenging efforts to cover the search area.
The response teams continue to coordinate and explore safe options to locate the missing individuals despite the difficult situation.
Authorities appealed to the public to pray for their safe recovery and for strength for their families.

articles.title: 30 rescued after tourist boat sinks off Manicani Island, Guiuan
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — Thirty passengers were rescued after a tourist boat carrying them from mainland Guiuan to Manicani Island in Eastern Samar submerged off Barangay Buenavista on Sunday, Aug. 30, the…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Thirty passengers were rescued after a tourist boat carrying them from mainland Guiuan to Manicani Island in Eastern Samar submerged off Barangay Buenavista on Sunday, Aug. 30, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) reported.

The passengers were rescued by local fisherfolk with assistance from tugboats MTUG Don Antonio Two and MTUG Joshmar III after the passenger motorbanca, identified as MBCA Vemstac 3, began taking in seawater at 10:50 a.m.

The PCG said the boat departed mainland Guiuan at 10:30 a.m. carrying 30 passengers bound for Barangay Buenavista. When it reached waters about 0.76 nautical mile from the shoreline, seawater reportedly entered through the rear portion of the vessel, causing it to gradually take in water before sinking.

Responding personnel from Coast Guard Station (CGS) South Eastern Samar, Coast Guard Sub-Station Guiuan, the Maritime Environmental Protection Unit-Eastern Samar and the Guiuan Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office arrived at the reported distress area at about 12:50 p.m.
By then, all 30 passengers had been safely brought ashore and had returned to their respective homes. No deaths or injuries were reported.

The PCG and Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office personnel later conducted surface monitoring in the area for possible oil or other pollutants from the submerged boat. No visible oil was observed on the water, although the vessel was reportedly carrying about 20 liters of diesel fuel.
The PCG also reported that the boat had departed mainland Guiuan without the required clearance from the agency.

An initial inquiry with boat captain and owner Tito Abucejo showed that the vessel was originally registered as RBCA Jalexa Zanicus. The owner had initiated the process of changing its name to MBCA Vemstac, but the change had not yet been approved by the proper authorities.
The 14.5-meter fiberglass-hulled boat was built in 2024, has a gross tonnage of 3.86 and is powered by a Mitsubishi engine.

The PCG advised Abucejo to fully cooperate with the ongoing investigation into the incident, including efforts to determine its cause, identify possible safety deficiencies and recommend measures to prevent similar maritime accidents.
Authorities are still verifying and consolidating the complete names and other details of the 30 passengers, who had already returned to their respective residences following the rescue. /mcm

articles.title: Student dies from ‘heat stroke’ during Agusan intramurals
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — A Grade 10 student died during school intramural activities in Cabadbaran City, Agusan del Norte, allegedly due to heat stroke. In an interview, Vilma Bag-ao said her…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — A Grade 10 student died during school intramural activities in Cabadbaran City, Agusan del Norte, allegedly due to heat stroke.
In an interview, Vilma Bag-ao said her son, Yusho Steve Bag-ao, a student at Mindanao Institute, was rushed to Cabadbaran District Hospital and declared dead around 4 p.m. on Aug. 26.
Bag-ao said doctors told the family that Yusho had suffered a heat stroke.

She later said his cause of death was ventricular tachyarrhythmia, or an abnormally rapid heart rhythm originating in the heart’s lower chambers, citing a medical abstract from Cabadbaran District Hospital.
Yusho had a congenital heart condition discovered when he was an infant, Bag-ao said. Doctors had previously recommended surgery but told the family it was not urgent.

His death occurred two weeks after extreme heat prompted Cabadbaran City Mayor Judy Chin Amante to suspend face-to-face classes in public schools on Aug. 12. Heat indices across parts of Caraga at the time ranged from 42 to 46 degrees Celsius.

Mindanao Institute also suspended classes because of the heat and advised students to stay hydrated and avoid unsafe heat exposure. The school later scheduled its Intramurals Meet and Buwan ng Wika activities for Aug. 24 to 28.
Bag-ao questioned the timing of the parental consent for her son’s participation in the intramurals.
She said Yusho’s father signed the consent form only after the students had already participated in a parade.
Bag-ao noted that the family has yet to receive a clear account of what happened after Yusho became ill, including whether CPR was performed before he was taken to the hospital.
The mother said she wants a clear explanation of what happened during her son’s final hours and whether adequate precautions were taken during the school activity. /mcm

articles.title: Thea Astley on her alleged involvement in Miles Ocampo-Elijah Canlas breakup: 'I would never do that'
articles.summary: After making headlines being seen together with Elijah Canlas, Thea Astley was accused by fans as to causing his breakup with Miles Ocampo. Thea was silent about it until she appeared on "Trggrd."…

blocks.text: Thea Astley (IMDB)
After making headlines being seen together with Elijah Canlas, Thea Astley was accused by fans as to causing his breakup with Miles Ocampo.
Thea was silent about it until she appeared on "Trggrd."
She admitted she was aware of the rumors.

"I think it was on our second or third day. We already saw na parang there was a video circulating, but we didn’t really think much of it at first until we got back sa Manila. And then, we saw how viral it had gotten and parang lumaki na siya nang lumaki,” Thea said.
Holding back her tears, Thea explained that the photo or video circulating online was taken out of context.
"Pag ‘yung screenshots lang talaga ‘yung tinignan mo, mapapaisip ka talaga that Jelo (Elijah) was like holding my hand or something like that," she said.
The actress went on to clarify there is nothing remotely romantic with his closeness to Elijah.

"Elijah and I are friends. Like we’ve been friends for years now at this point, and I would never go on a trip like that if, like, alam mo ‘yun. I’ve never cheated on anyone. I’ve never been the third party in any relationship to my knowledge,” she added.
Thea added that she understands why fans are quick to blame her for Elijah and Miles' split.
"Nakita nila paano nag-blossom ‘yung relationship ng dalawa through the years and then to suddenly parang I here I come na parang threat to that bond," she said.

"I would never do that to another girl. I know what that’s like. I know what that feeling is like. I would never ever willingly come between a relationship. Never. I would never do that," she concluded.

articles.title: Baguio police to step up security amid fears of retaliation linked to bullying incident
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) has committed to implementing security measures in response to reports of possible retaliation following a bullying incident at Pinget National High…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) has committed to implementing security measures in response to reports of possible retaliation following a bullying incident at Pinget National High School, aiming to ensure the safety of all those involved.

BCPO City Director PCol. Ruel Tagel stated that protective measures would be implemented for all parties involved to guarantee their safety while authorities assess reports suggesting a risk of retaliation.
He noted an increase in statements and strong calls for retaliation on social media following the incident.

Tagel assured that they would remain vigilant and strive to ensure the safety of everyone involved. "We will deploy additional police personnel to conduct regular patrols around Pinget National High School."
He mentioned that the school had requested increased police presence from BCPO Station 2, as well as active patrolling by the barangays surrounding the school, to help prevent similar incidents.

Meanwhile, City Social Welfare and Development Officer Liza Bulayungan stated that the barangays of Pinget, Pinsao Proper, and Pinsao Pilot have also pledged to strengthen community-level interventions for child protection.

"All participating agencies, school officials, and parents have pledged to uphold accountability, rehabilitation, monitoring, and, above all, the protection of the children's rights and welfare; they will also ensure the safety of the victim, the respondents, their families, school staff, and other community members while the case is being addressed through the proper mechanisms," stated Balungayan.

articles.title: PH Coast Guard on heightened alert as ‘habagat’ continues to threaten Northern Luzon
articles.summary: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — The Philippine Coast Guard–Northwestern Luzon has placed its units on heightened alert as the enhanced southwest monsoon, or habagat, continued to dump heavy rains…

blocks.text: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — The Philippine Coast Guard–Northwestern Luzon has placed its units on heightened alert as the enhanced southwest monsoon, or habagat, continued to dump heavy rains across Northern Luzon.

Lieutenant Junior Grade Dado M. Ab-abulon Jr., officer-in-charge of the Coast Guard District North Western Luzon Community Relations Office, said Coast Guard stations and sub-stations have been placed on alert to ensure the immediate deployment of personnel in areas that may be affected by flooding and other weather-related emergencies.
Ab-abulon said 60 response groups composed of around 400 Coast Guard personnel are ready for deployment.
The Coast Guard has also prepared 10 land assets and 28 floating assets for search-and-rescue operations, maritime patrols, and evacuation missions.
Ports, rivers, and other critical areas in the region are being closely monitored as heavy rains continue.

The heightened alert came as the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) warned of a rainy start to September, with several provinces in Northern Luzon expected to receive between 100 and 200 millimeters of rain.
In Weather Advisory No. 30 issued at 5 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 30, PAGASA placed Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga under the 100- to 200-mm rainfall outlook.
Abra, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, and several nearby provinces may receive between 50 and 100 mm of rain.
PAGASA warned that rainfall could be higher in mountainous and elevated areas and that the danger of flooding and landslides could worsen in areas already saturated by previous rains.
The heavy rainfall is expected to persist through Tuesday.
On Monday, the 100- to 200-mm rainfall outlook will cover Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan.
By Tuesday, Sept. 1, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Abra, Benguet, and Zambales are still expected to receive between 100 and 200 mm of rain.
The Coast Guard advised residents, particularly fishermen and travelers, to avoid unnecessary travel and closely monitor weather bulletins and advisories from authorities.
Ab-abulon also urged the public to remain calm, comply with evacuation orders, and immediately coordinate with the nearest Coast Guard station in case of emergencies.
The Coast Guard is continuing to coordinate with local government units and other government agencies to ensure a swift response to weather-related incidents. (Freddie G. Lazaro)
